$ sha256 of ~/.vscode/extensions/farmountain.hipcortex-memory-3.12.0/server/win32/hipcortex-windows-amd64.exe -> 2CB5CCC6 at 8642048 bytes, identical to the 3.11.0 folder copy, and the ASCII scan finds 3.11.0 in it and not 3.12.0
questions.resolution: Published is correct and the drift is local. The released 3.12.0 VSIX and the released standalone binary both carry a server that answers 3.12.0, so EXPECTED_SERVER_VERSION is satisfiable and no channel is mislabelled. The one installation on this machine was a silent partial upgrade: the extension host and package.json reached 3.12.0 while the whole server payload stayed at 3.11.0, because the upgrade ran against a server that held its own executable open. The installed payload was replaced with the published 3.12.0 files at hash parity, without stopping the running process, so the listener keeps answering 3.11.0 until it is restarted.
questions.doesNotEstablish: That a VSIX install completes its server payload atomically - the failure mode is a file lock held by the process being upgraded, which no test in either repository exercises. It says nothing about the other installed versions of this extension, which were not examined, and it does not establish that a restart alone suffices on a machine where strictServerVersion is enabled.

questions.question: Is a channel-alignment claim testable by comparing versions inside manifests, or does it need a probe of the artifact that is actually distributed?
artifactsTried: package.json, public/manifest.json and src/types/index.ts -> three copies of one version number, checkable by string comparison alone
tests/quality/manifest.spec.ts -> reads the source manifest, so it can prove the repository agrees with itself and cannot see a packaged or installed artifact
the distributed VSIX and the running listener -> the only two surfaces that can disagree with every file in the repository
evidence: $ npm run verify -> 53 spec files and 823 tests, all of which read source, and none of which reads a release asset

$ hash-and-diff of the installed extension tree against the extracted published VSIX -> dist/extension.js byte-identical at 295768 bytes, package.json equal once the installer metadata is ignored, and six server payload files different
$ npm run test:clarity -> the gate reads this ledger, so the finding is recorded rather than asserted in prose
questions.resolution: Manifest comparison is necessary and not sufficient. It proves the repository agrees with itself, which is what it did: every source surface said 3.12.0 while the installed artifact answered 3.11.0. A claim that a channel is aligned therefore needs one probe of the distributed artifact, which is what the evidence for Q21 performs, and this entry records that no existing gate reaches it.
questions.doesNotEstablish: That such a probe belongs in npm run verify - it needs a released artifact and a running listener, neither of which a unit gate may assume. It also does not establish a general check for the other distribution channels.

questions.question: Is the zip the release page publishes conformant with the ZIP specification, and does any gate in this repository inspect it?
artifactsTried: hipcortex-chrome-extension-v0.1.0.zip -> opened with System.IO.Compression and 168 entries listed
scripts/package.js -> the Windows leg called Compress-Archive, which emits backslash entry names
tests/quality/gates.spec.ts -> asserts only that package.js is reached through Node, and never reads the archive it produces
evidence: $ entry-name scan of the released zip -> 148 of 168 names contained a backslash and 0 contained a forward slash
$ node scripts/package.js then the same scan -> 148 forward slashes, 0 backslashes, manifest.json at the root
$ npm test -> tests/quality/zip.spec.ts pins the separator, the root manifest.json and the recoverable bytes
$ gh release download v0.1.0 then an entry-level comparison against a fresh build -> 168 entries on both sides, 0 size differences, 0 CRC-32 differences
$ sha256 of the two files -> 3CC6F6EB for the download and 6CC9DEDB for the fresh build, which differ because the writer stamps every entry with its build time
questions.resolution: Not conformant, and nothing reached it. APPNOTE 4.4.17.1 names the forward slash as the entry separator; Compress-Archive on Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes backslashes, and the extension loads from dist/ either way, so no loadability test could observe it. The archive is now written by scripts/zip.js, which has no platform leg, and the script refuses to emit a backslash name or an archive whose manifest is not at the root.
questions.doesNotEstablish: That the store rejects a backslash archive - the defect was removed before uploading, so the tolerance of the pipeline is untested. It also says nothing about the policy review the archive must still pass.

questions.question: Are the icons in the package real images at the sizes the manifest declares?
artifactsTried: dist/icons/*.png -> four files of 70 bytes each
scripts/copy-assets.js -> wrote one base64 1x1 transparent PNG to all four filenames
tests/quality/manifest.spec.ts -> asserted the four paths exist and never read a dimension
evidence: $ System.Drawing measurement of the four packaged icons -> 1x1 for all four, 70 bytes each
$ store documentation on the icon requirement -> a 128x128 PNG is mandatory inside the archive
$ npm run verify after the fix -> the dimension and pixel assertions pass against 128x128 at 353 bytes
questions.resolution: Not real images. The build wrote a 1x1 stub to every filename, which satisfies the manifest's path check and fails the store's icon requirement, so the package could not be submitted at all. The icons are now committed artwork in public/icons/, copied to dist/icons/ by the same asset step as every other file, at 16, 32, 48 and 128 pixels, and each one's dimensions are asserted from its own IHDR chunk.
questions.doesNotEstablish: That the artwork is a brand asset - the four files are geometric placeholders with transparent padding and must be replaced before the listing goes public. It also does not establish that the store accepts their alpha and framing.

questions.question: The manifest declares six optional provider hosts. Does anything ever request them at runtime, and is that a defect?
artifactsTried: public/manifest.json - optional_host_permissions names the six provider origins; host_permissions names only 127.0.0.1 and localhost
src/** - a search for the permissions API found no call site
docs/END-STATE.md - G1.9 requires the declaration to name every canonical host
.github/instructions/mv3-extension.instructions.md - stated that the hosts are requested at runtime
evidence: $ git grep chrome.permissions over src/ -> no match, so no runtime request exists anywhere in the shipped code
$ git grep permissions.request over src/ -> no match
$ npm test -> tests/quality/manifest.spec.ts passes with the six hosts declared, which is the test G1.9 names
$ npm run verify after correcting the instruction file and writing the store runbook -> 55 test files passed
questions.resolution: Nothing requests them, and that is not a defect. Capture on those origins is granted at install time by content_scripts.matches, not by a runtime permission request, so the optional declaration is inert. It stays because G1.9 requires it and manifest.spec.ts fails without it. The instruction file was wrong to describe a runtime request and has been corrected; the store runbook now answers the question before a reviewer asks it.
questions.doesNotEstablish: That the store accepts an optional declaration nothing calls - the package has not been uploaded, so the review outcome is untested. It also does not establish that capture works on any provider page; that is the browser gate 8.12, which no test in this repository can reach.

questions.question: The archive pins the extension ID with a key field. Does the Chrome Web Store accept a package that carries that field?
artifactsTried: the Developer Dashboard upload of hipcortex-chrome-extension-v0.1.0.zip - the whole file was refused
https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/manifest/key - the documented order is the reverse: upload without the field, then copy the public key the dashboard shows into it
scripts/install-host.mjs - derives the ID from the key, so allowed_origins can name an extension that has never been loaded
tests/host/registration.spec.ts - asserts the shipped manifest pins a usable key, so deleting the field would fail the gate
scripts/package.js and scripts/zip.js - the only place the upload archive is written, and so the only place the field can be removed without touching dist/
evidence: $ upload of the v0.1.0 archive to the Developer Dashboard -> There was a problem uploading your file: key field is not allowed in manifest
$ npm run package then an independent read of the archive with System.IO.Compression -> entries=168 backslash=0 rootManifest=1 and the archived manifest has no key field
$ node -e import of scripts/install-host.mjs -> defaultExtensionId() still returns eklnpdcephecmddelagbablmeajoogkf, because dist/manifest.json keeps the field
$ npx vitest run tests/quality/zip.spec.ts -> 11 passed, four of them pinning the removal, the byte pass-through of every other entry and the no-op case
$ gh release upload v0.1.0 --clobber then gh release download v0.1.0 -> the published asset is byte-identical to the built file, 229710 bytes, and its manifest carries no key
$ npm run verify -> Test Files 55 passed, Tests 848 passed, exit 0
questions.resolution: Not accepted, and the field had to go - but not from dist/. The store refuses any package whose manifest carries a key and derives the published item's ID from a public key it generates itself, so the store ID will not be the pinned one. The field is therefore stripped from the archived manifest only, by storeSafeEntries in scripts/zip.js, which package.js applies and then checks; dist/manifest.json keeps it, because the native host's allowed_origins is derived from it. README.md, docs/STORE.md, docs/PRIVACY.md, docs/PROTOCOL.md, docs/END-STATE.md and the MV3 instruction file now say which of the two IDs each statement is about, and section 11 of docs/STORE.md records the post-upload step that replaces the key with the store's public key and re-registers the host.
questions.doesNotEstablish: That the store accepts the corrected archive - the upload is manual and has not been retried. It also does not establish the published item's ID, which the store assigns on first upload and which therefore remains unknown; that is why the post-upload step exists. And it does not establish that a store installation reaches the core, because the key replacement and the host re-registration are steps a person performs.
